name: Abhishek Cauligi
title: Assistant Professor; Principal Investigator, Autonomous Control & Exploration Lab
fitReason: Direct machine-learning/optimization integration for autonomous robots, including an executed neural-warm-start planner in space, with an active new academic group and aerial test facility.

physicalEvidence.summary: The November 2025 primary paper reports February 2025 flight tests on NASA Astrobee aboard the ISS, plus ground tests at NASA Ames. A supervised feedforward network supplies trajectory initializations; GuSTO sequential convex programming enforces constraints and the robot executes the result. The flight session executed 18 trajectories, with onboard network inference. This is Stanford/NASA collaborative hardware predating the July 2025 JHU start, not JHU-owned Astrobee equipment. July 2026 Robodrome infrastructure is current, but planned local ML flight work is not counted as a completed new deployment.

shortVisit.summary: Current ACE joining page covers PhD applicants and undergraduate/MS students already at JHU. General collaboration and open lab-meeting wording does not establish an external-master’s visitor appointment. The current roster includes a visiting Fulbright PhD student, which is scoped precedent only.

scoreReasons.fit: Substantive neural trajectory optimization and safe autonomous robot decision-making.
scoreReasons.physical: Concrete 2025 flight execution, but on prior/collaborative NASA–Stanford hardware; new JHU infrastructure does not prove a completed local learned deployment.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: No current external-master’s short-visitor invitation; visiting PhD precedent earns no points.
scoreReasons.freshness: Official July 2026 Robodrome activity and current 2026 laboratory publications/people, distinguished from the February 2025 flight date.

name: Joseph Moore
title: Assistant Professor; Director, Agile and Intelligent Robotics Laboratory
fitReason: Strong safe RL and real-robot navigation overlap: learned value functions augment a statistical MPC controller, rather than remaining purely theoretical.

physicalEvidence.summary: June 2025 primary revision of the ACC 2025 study executes PAC-NMPC with an RL-trained perception-based value function on a physical 1/10-scale Traxxas Rally Car using Velodyne Puck LITE LiDAR in a motion-capture barrel-obstacle area. The same paper’s fixed-wing learned navigation results are simulations, not physical flight. The work originated in 2023 and spans JHU/APL collaborators; current AIRO roster includes its graduate authors. July 2026 Robodrome confirms local aerial infrastructure but not a new completed RL flight experiment.

shortVisit.summary: Current official faculty and AIRO pages establish PI status, graduate/MSE advisees and active 2025 publication news. No explicit external-master’s summer visitor or internship invitation found in the reviewed public pages.

scoreReasons.fit: Direct safe RL, learned perception/value inference and computational robot control.
scoreReasons.physical: Named physical car and executed learned-value MPC, with older/collaborative origins rather than a newly verified own-lab 2026 learning experiment.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: No current external short-visitor invitation verified.
scoreReasons.freshness: July 2026 official facility activity, current roster and ACC 2025 research; no claim that the car experiments occurred in 2026.
